subject: Computer Networks & Security
exam_relevance: 8-10 questions expected in BPSC TRE CS exam

questions.question: How many layers does the OSI reference model have?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) model has 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for physical transmission of raw bits over a communication channel?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Physical layer (Layer 1) handles transmission of raw bits over the physical medium, defining hardware specifications like cables and voltages.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for framing, error detection, and MAC addressing?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Data Link Layer (Layer 2) handles framing, error detection/correction, and MAC addressing. It is divided into LLC and MAC sublayers.

questions.question: The MAC (Media Access Control) sublayer is part of which OSI layer?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: MAC sublayer is the lower sublayer of the Data Link Layer (Layer 2). It controls how devices on a network gain access to the medium.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for logical addressing (IP addresses) and routing?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Network Layer (Layer 3) provides logical addressing (IP) and routing — it determines the best path for data to travel across networks.

questions.question: Which OSI layer provides end-to-end communication, flow control, and error recovery?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Transport Layer (Layer 4) provides end-to-end communication, segmentation, flow control, and error recovery. TCP and UDP operate here.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for establishing, managing, and terminating sessions between applications?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Session Layer (Layer 5) establishes, manages, and terminates communication sessions between applications on different devices.

questions.question: Which OSI layer handles data encryption, compression, and format conversion?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Presentation Layer (Layer 6) handles data translation, encryption, decryption, and compression — it ensures data is in usable format.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is closest to the end user and provides network services to user applications?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Application Layer (Layer 7) is the topmost layer and provides interfaces for end users and applications like HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS.

questions.question: In the OSI model, which layer converts data into signals suitable for transmission?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Physical Layer converts data bits into electrical, optical, or radio signals for transmission over the physical medium.

questions.question: The process of adding headers and trailers at each OSI layer is called:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Encapsulation is the process of adding protocol headers/trailers at each OSI layer as data moves from Application down to Physical layer.

questions.question: Which two sublayers does the Data Link Layer consist of?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Data Link Layer is divided into LLC (Logical Link Control) for error control and MAC (Media Access Control) for channel access.

questions.question: What is the Protocol Data Unit (PDU) at the Transport layer called?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: PDU names: Physical=Bits, Data Link=Frame, Network=Packet, Transport=Segment, Session/Presentation/Application=Data/Message.

questions.question: At which OSI layer does a Router primarily operate?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Routers operate at the Network Layer (Layer 3), using IP addresses to forward packets between different networks.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for port addressing and multiplexing?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Transport Layer uses port numbers to identify processes (multiplexing). TCP/UDP port numbers allow multiple services on one IP address.

questions.question: How many layers does the TCP/IP model have?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The TCP/IP model has 4 layers: Network Access (Link), Internet, Transport, and Application. Unlike OSI's 7 layers.

questions.question: Which TCP/IP layer corresponds to both the Physical and Data Link layers of the OSI model?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Network Access (Link) layer in TCP/IP combines OSI's Physical and Data Link layers, handling hardware addressing and media access.

questions.question: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is best described as:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented (uses 3-way handshake), reliable (acknowledgements, retransmission), and provides ordered delivery.

questions.question: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is described as:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless (no handshake), unreliable (no acknowledgements), but faster. Used for DNS, video streaming, online gaming.

questions.question: Which protocol provides reliable, ordered delivery using a three-way handshake?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: TCP uses a 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) to establish a connection before data transfer, ensuring reliability and order.

questions.question: Which layer of the TCP/IP model is responsible for routing packets across networks?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Internet Layer (equivalent to OSI Network layer) handles logical addressing and routing using IP. Contains IP, ICMP, ARP protocols.

questions.question: ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) operates at which TCP/IP layer?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: ICMP operates at the Internet Layer. It is used for error reporting and diagnostics (e.g., the ping command uses ICMP echo requests).

questions.question: The ping command is used to test network connectivity. Which of the following is true about ping?

options.B: It uses ICMP echo request and reply
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Ping uses ICMP echo request/reply (not TCP) and summarizes round-trip time and packet loss stats. Both B and C are correct.

questions.question: Which TCP/IP layer corresponds to the Session, Presentation, and Application layers of the OSI model?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: TCP/IP's Application layer combines OSI's Session, Presentation, and Application layers. Contains HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly maps OSI layers to TCP/IP layers?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three mappings (A, B, C) are correct: OSI Network=TCP/IP Internet; OSI Transport=TCP/IP Transport; OSI Phy+DL=TCP/IP Network Access.

questions.question: What is the default port number for HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: HTTP uses port 80 for unencrypted web traffic. HTTPS uses port 443. FTP uses ports 20 (data) and 21 (control).

questions.question: Which port is used by HTTPS (HTTP Secure)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: HTTPS (HTTP over SSL/TLS) uses port 443. It is the secure version of HTTP that encrypts communication between browser and server.

questions.question: FTP uses which two port numbers?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: FTP uses port 21 for control (commands) and port 20 for data transfer. Both ports are needed for full FTP operation.

questions.question: Which port number is used by SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: SMTP uses port 25. It is used to send emails. POP3 uses port 110, IMAP uses port 143 — both for receiving emails.

questions.question: Which protocol and port is used for secure remote login to a server?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) on port 22 provides encrypted remote login. Telnet on port 23 is insecure (unencrypted) predecessor to SSH.

questions.question: Which port does DNS (Domain Name System) use?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: DNS uses port 53 for both UDP (queries) and TCP (zone transfers). It resolves domain names to IP addresses.

questions.question: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) uses which port?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: POP3 uses port 110. It downloads emails from server to client and usually deletes them from the server. IMAP (143) keeps emails on server.

questions.question: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) uses which port number?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: IMAP uses port 143. Unlike POP3 (port 110), IMAP keeps emails on the server and allows access from multiple devices.

questions.question: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) uses which port numbers?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: DHCP uses port 67 for server (receives client requests) and port 68 for client (receives server responses). It auto-assigns IP addresses.

questions.question: Which port does RIP (Routing Information Protocol) use?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: RIP uses UDP port 520. It is a distance-vector routing protocol that uses hop count as the metric (max 15 hops).

questions.question: When a mail server sends mail to other mail servers, it acts as:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: When sending mail to another server, the mail server acts as an SMTP client. The receiving server acts as SMTP server.

questions.question: Telnet operates on which port number?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Telnet uses port 23. It provides remote login but transmits data in plaintext (unencrypted), making it insecure. SSH (port 22) replaced it.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols operate at the Application layer of the TCP/IP model?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: HTTP, FTP, and SMTP all operate at the Application layer of TCP/IP. All three are correct, so D (More than one) is the answer.

questions.question: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) is used to:

options.A: Resolve IP address to MAC address
options.C: Resolve domain name to IP address
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: ARP resolves IP addresses to MAC (hardware) addresses. DNS resolves domain names to IPs. DHCP assigns IP addresses to hosts.

questions.question: DNS (Domain Name System) primarily performs which function?

options.B: Resolves domain names to IP addresses
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: DNS translates human-readable domain names (e.g., www.google.com) to IP addresses. It is the internet's phone book.

questions.question: An IPv4 address is how many bits long?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long, written as four octets in dotted-decimal notation (e.g., 192.168.1.1). Range: 0.0.0.0 to 255.255.255.255.

questions.question: Class A IPv4 addresses have their first octet in which range?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Class A: 0-127 (first bit = 0). Class B: 128-191 (first bits = 10). Class C: 192-223 (first bits = 110). Class D: 224-239 (multicast).

questions.question: Class B IPv4 addresses start with which range in the first octet?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Class B addresses have 128-191 as the first octet. They support up to 65,534 hosts per network. Used by medium to large organizations.

questions.question: Which class of IPv4 addresses is used for multicasting?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Class D (224.0.0.0 to 239.255.255.255) is reserved for multicasting. Class E (240-255) is reserved for research/experimental use.

questions.question: Which of the following is a private IP address range?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three are private IP ranges per RFC 1918: Class A (10.x.x.x), Class B (172.16-31.x.x), Class C (192.168.x.x). All correct → D.

questions.question: What is the default subnet mask for a Class C network?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Class C default subnet mask is 255.255.255.0 (/24). Class A: 255.0.0.0 (/8). Class B: 255.255.0.0 (/16).

questions.question: The loopback address in IPv4 is:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 127.0.0.1 (localhost) is the loopback address used to test the TCP/IP stack on the local machine without sending data to any external network.

questions.question: How many usable host addresses are available in a /24 subnet?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A /24 subnet has 256 addresses (2^8), minus 2 (network and broadcast) = 254 usable host addresses.

questions.question: Which class of IPv4 supports the largest number of hosts per network?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Class A has 24 bits for host ID, supporting 2^24 - 2 = 16,777,214 hosts per network. Largest host capacity among standard classes.

questions.question: The IP address 172.20.5.10 belongs to which class?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 172 falls in the range 128-191, so 172.20.5.10 is a Class B address. It also falls in the private range 172.16.0.0-172.31.255.255.

questions.question: NAT (Network Address Translation) is primarily used to:

options.C: Allow private IP addresses to access the internet
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: NAT translates private IP addresses to public IP addresses, allowing multiple private hosts to share a single public IP address for internet access.

questions.question: The purpose of a subnet mask in TCP/IP networking is:

options.A: To identify the network portion of an IP address
options.B: To determine if two hosts are on the same network
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Subnet mask identifies the network portion of an IP address AND is used to determine if a host is on the same or different network. Both A and B are correct.

questions.question: An IPv6 address is how many bits long?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long, written as 8 groups of 4 hexadecimal digits separated by colons. This allows 2^128 unique addresses.

questions.question: An IPv6 address is written as how many groups of hexadecimal digits?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: IPv6 is written as 8 groups of 4 hexadecimal digits separated by colons (e.g., 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334).

questions.question: Which technique allows IPv4 and IPv6 to coexist on the same network device?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Dual Stack allows a device to run both IPv4 and IPv6 simultaneously. Tunneling encapsulates IPv6 within IPv4. Both are IPv6 transition mechanisms.

questions.question: IPv6 provides which advantages over IPv4?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: IPv6 offers larger address space, built-in security (IPSec), simplified header, stateless auto-configuration (SLAAC). All A, B, C are advantages.

questions.question: In IPv6 header translation, which statement is correct regarding the IPv6 flow label?

options.A: IPv6 flow label is directly converted to IPv4 flow label
options.B: IPv6 header is smaller than IPv4 header
options.C: IPv6 flow label field has no equivalent in IPv4 header
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: IPv6 flow label (20-bit) has no equivalent in IPv4. During header translation, flow labels cannot be directly mapped — they are discarded.

questions.question: IPv6 uses which technique to send IPv6 packets through IPv4 networks?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Tunneling encapsulates IPv6 packets inside IPv4 packets to traverse IPv4 networks. This is one of the IPv4-to-IPv6 transition mechanisms.

questions.question: The IPv6 loopback address is:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: ::1 is the IPv6 loopback address (equivalent to 127.0.0.1 in IPv4). It represents 0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001.

questions.question: IPv6 addresses use how many bytes (octets)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: IPv6 is 128 bits = 16 bytes (octets). Each hex digit represents 4 bits, so 128 bits = 32 hex digits arranged in 8 groups of 4.

questions.question: At which OSI layer does a Hub operate?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A hub operates at the Physical Layer (Layer 1). It broadcasts data to all ports — it has no intelligence to filter based on MAC or IP addresses.

questions.question: At which OSI layer does a Switch primarily operate?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A switch operates at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2). It uses MAC addresses to forward frames only to the destination port, unlike a hub.

questions.question: The primary function of a router is:

options.A: To connect multiple networks and route packets
options.C: To filter frames using MAC addresses
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Router's primary function is to connect multiple networks and determine the best path to route packets. It operates at the Network Layer (Layer 3).

questions.question: A gateway operates at which layer(s) of the OSI model?

options.B: All layers (can work up to Application layer)
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A gateway can operate at all 7 OSI layers (most commonly Transport and Application layers). It connects networks with different protocols.

questions.question: A repeater operates at which OSI layer and what is its function?

options.B: Data Link Layer — filters MAC addresses
options.C: Physical Layer — regenerates and amplifies signals
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A repeater operates at the Physical Layer (Layer 1). It regenerates and amplifies the signal to extend the network's physical range.

questions.question: A bridge operates at which OSI layer?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A bridge operates at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2). It connects two LAN segments and uses MAC addresses to filter and forward frames.

questions.question: What is the size of a MAC (Media Access Control) address?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A MAC address is 48 bits (6 bytes) long, written as 12 hexadecimal digits (e.g., 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E). First 24 bits: OUI, last 24 bits: device ID.

questions.question: A NIC (Network Interface Card) operates at which layers?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: NIC operates at both Physical and Data Link Layers. It has a MAC address (Data Link) and handles physical signal transmission (Physical layer).

questions.question: Which device uses MAC address table to forward frames only to the correct port?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A switch maintains a MAC address table (CAM table) to intelligently forward frames only to the correct destination port, reducing collisions.

questions.question: Which device would you use to connect a LAN to the internet?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A router connects different networks (like a LAN to the internet). It routes packets between networks using IP addresses at Layer 3.

questions.question: Which of the following is a guided (wired) transmission media?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Fiber optic cable is guided (wired) media. Microwave and radio waves are unguided (wireless) media. Guided media includes twisted pair, coax, fiber.

questions.question: Which transmission medium provides the highest bandwidth and is immune to electromagnetic interference?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Fiber optic cable uses light pulses, providing the highest bandwidth, longest range, and immunity to electromagnetic interference (EMI).

questions.question: Twisted pair cable is widely used in which type of network?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Twisted pair (Cat5e, Cat6) is the most common medium for LANs. It is inexpensive and easy to install. Ethernet uses twisted pair cables.

questions.question: Which unguided medium uses line-of-sight transmission and is used for satellite communication?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Microwave uses line-of-sight transmission and is used for satellite and long-distance communication. It cannot pass through buildings.

questions.question: Infrared transmission is typically used for:

options.A: Short-range communication like TV remotes and IrDA
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Infrared is used for short-range, line-of-sight communication such as TV remotes, IrDA port transfers. It cannot pass through walls.

questions.question: Coaxial cable consists of which layers (from inner to outer)?

options.A: Two twisted copper wires with insulation
options.B: Inner conductor, insulating layer, metallic shield, outer jacket
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Coaxial cable has: inner conductor → insulating layer → metallic mesh shield → outer plastic jacket. Option B describes twisted pair, C describes fiber.

questions.question: Which category of UTP cable supports Gigabit Ethernet (1000BASE-T)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Cat 5e and Cat 6 support Gigabit Ethernet. Cat 5 supports up to 100 Mbps. Cat 3 supports 10 Mbps. Cat 6 supports 10 Gbps at shorter lengths.

questions.question: Which of the following about fiber optic cable is true?

options.A: It transmits data as light pulses
options.B: It is immune to electromagnetic interference
options.C: It supports much higher bandwidth than copper cables
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three statements about fiber optic are true: transmits light pulses, immune to EMI, and provides much higher bandwidth than copper. Answer is D.

questions.question: In which network topology does every device connect to a central hub or switch?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Star topology, all devices connect to a central hub or switch. It is the most common LAN topology — easy to manage but central point of failure.

questions.question: In a Bus topology, all devices share a single communication line called:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Bus topology, all devices share a single backbone cable. Data travels in both directions. A failure in the backbone affects the entire network.

questions.question: In a Ring topology, data travels in which manner?

options.A: Data is broadcast to all devices simultaneously
options.B: Data travels in one direction (unidirectional) through each node
options.C: Data is routed via the central hub
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Ring topology, each device connects to two others, forming a ring. Data travels in one direction (or bidirectional in dual ring) through each node.

questions.question: In a Mesh topology, every device is connected to every other device. For N nodes, how many connections are needed in a full mesh?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Full mesh requires N(N-1)/2 connections. For 5 nodes: 5×4/2=10 connections. It offers highest redundancy but is expensive to implement.

questions.question: Which network topology is a combination of two or more different topologies?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Hybrid topology combines two or more different topologies (e.g., Star-Bus, Star-Ring). Most real-world networks use hybrid topologies.

questions.question: Tree topology is a variation of which basic topology?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Tree topology is a hierarchical variation of Star topology. Multiple star networks are connected to a backbone bus, forming a tree structure.

questions.question: Which topology provides the highest fault tolerance and redundancy?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Mesh topology provides the highest fault tolerance. Full mesh has multiple paths between any two devices, so if one link fails, others remain active.

questions.question: The main disadvantage of Star topology is:

options.A: Data collision on the single cable
options.C: Single point of failure at the central hub/switch
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Star topology's main disadvantage is the central hub/switch is a single point of failure — if it fails, the entire network goes down.

questions.question: Which topology is easiest to install and most commonly used in modern LANs?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Star topology is the most commonly used in modern LANs. It is easy to install, troubleshoot, and manage. Used with Ethernet switches.

questions.question: Which network topology requires the most cabling?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Full Mesh requires N(N-1)/2 cables, the most of any topology. For 10 devices, that's 45 connections. Very expensive but most redundant.

questions.question: In symmetric key cryptography, the same key is used for:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Symmetric key cryptography uses the SAME key for both encryption and decryption. Examples: DES, AES, 3DES. Key must be securely shared.

questions.question: In asymmetric key cryptography, who keeps the private key?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In asymmetric cryptography, the receiver keeps the private key (for decryption). The public key is shared openly. Sender uses public key to encrypt.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a symmetric key encryption algorithm?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: AES (and DES, 3DES) are symmetric algorithms. RSA and Diffie-Hellman are asymmetric. AES is currently the most widely used encryption standard.

questions.question: RSA is an example of which type of encryption?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman) is an asymmetric public-key encryption algorithm. It uses a pair of keys: public key (encrypt) and private key (decrypt).

questions.question: A computer virus has which essential ability that distinguishes it from other malware?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A computer virus's essential and defining ability is to replicate/clone itself by attaching to other files. This self-replication distinguishes it from other malware.

questions.question: Which of the following would breach system integrity?

options.C: Full access rights for all users
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Giving all users full access rights violates the principle of least privilege and breaches system integrity. Users should only have permissions they need.

questions.question: A firewall in network security is used to:

options.C: Monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A firewall monitors and controls network traffic based on predefined security rules. It acts as a barrier between trusted internal and untrusted external networks.

questions.question: A digital signature provides which security services?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Digital signatures provide authentication, non-repudiation, and data integrity. All three options A, B, C are correct services provided by digital signatures.

questions.question: DES (Data Encryption Standard) uses which key length?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: DES uses a 56-bit key (64-bit with 8 parity bits). It is now considered insecure due to short key length. AES replaced it — 128, 192, or 256-bit keys.

questions.question: Which type of attack involves an attacker intercepting communication between two parties without their knowledge?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack involves intercepting communication between two parties. The attacker can eavesdrop or alter the communication.

questions.question: SSL/TLS protocols are used to provide security for which application?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: SSL/TLS primarily secures HTTPS web traffic. HTTPS = HTTP + SSL/TLS encryption on port 443. It ensures confidentiality and authentication on the web.

questions.question: In public-key (asymmetric) cryptography, if Alice wants to send a secret message to Bob, she should encrypt it with:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: To send a secret message to Bob, Alice encrypts with BOB's public key. Only Bob's private key can decrypt it. Alice's private key is used for digital signatures.
